320041.title: Convex-ear decomposition inheritance for rank-selected face posets
320041.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a $(d-1)$-dimensional complex admitting a convex-ear decomposition, and let $S\subseteq [d]$. Write $P_\Sigma$ for the face poset of $\Sigma$, and $(P_\Sigma)_S$ for its rank-selected subposet; let $\Delta((P_\Sigma)_S)$ denote the order complex of this subposet. **Convex-ear decomposition inheritance claim.** The complex

$$
\Delta((P_\Sigma)_S)
$$

admits a convex-ear decomposition. The claim gives a sufficient condition for rank-selected order complexes of face posets to retain convex-ear decompositions; the surrounding text notes that the analogous assertion can fail when $d\in S$, so the precise range of the theorem and its hypotheses are important.
320041.source_name: Jay Schweig, “Convex-Ear Decompositions and the Flag h-Vector”, arXiv:1006.2561 (2010).
320041.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2006–2010). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0605238](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605238).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.2561

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2010).

375611.title: Negami's Planar Cover Conjecture
375611.statement: Let $G$ be a connected finite simple graph. A **finite planar cover** of $G$ is a finite graph that covers $G$ in the graph-theoretic sense, with the covering graph planar. **Negami's Planar Cover Conjecture.** The graph $G$ has a finite planar cover if and only if it can be embedded on the projective plane. The sufficiency is clear, while the necessity remains open; the rotation-compatible version has already been proved.
375611.source_name: Shohei Koizumi, Yusuke Suzuki and Kensuke Tamura, “Another proof of the result on rotation compatible planar covers”, arXiv:2606.27703 (2026).
375611.references:
**5 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2006–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2412.10023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10023), [arXiv:2412.19560](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19560), [arXiv:1108.0064](https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.0064), [arXiv:math/0612342](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0612342).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27703

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2026). “In the conjecture above, the sufficiency is clear, but the necessity is still open.”

379539.title: The component-isomorphism conjecture for polynomial digraphs
379539.statement: Let $\Phi(x,y)$ be a standard polynomial of partial degree $d$. Let $G(\Phi)$ be its associated polynomial digraph, and let $G(\Phi)^*$ denote the nonsingular part of this digraph. Suppose that $H$ is a $d$-regular digraph isomorphic to a component of $G(\Phi)^*$. **Component-isomorphism conjecture.** All components of $G(\Phi)^*$ are isomorphic to $H$. This conjecture is motivated by cases in which $\Phi$ is homogeneous, has partial degree one, or is symmetric of partial and total degree two, where the components have been shown to be mutually isomorphic. The general assertion for standard polynomials of partial degree $d$ is left open in the source.
379539.source_name: Josep M. Brunat and Antonio Montes, “On polynomial digraphs”, arXiv:math/0601731 (2006).
379539.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601731

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2006).

379541.title: Sturmfels–Ziegler extension-space conjecture for realizable oriented matroids
379541.statement: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a realizable oriented matroid of rank $r$. Its extension space is the simplicial complex associated to the natural poset of one-point extensions of $\mathcal{M}$. **Sturmfels–Ziegler extension-space conjecture.** The extension space of $\mathcal{M}$ is homotopy equivalent to a sphere of dimension $r-1$. The source presents this as an open conjecture relevant to the study of lifting triangulations and oriented matroids; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
379541.source_name: Francisco Santos, “Geometric bistellar flips. The setting, the context and a construction”, arXiv:math/0601746 (2006).
379541.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601746

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2006).

379564.title: The exchange-graph independence conjecture for cluster algebras
379564.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y},B)$ be a cluster algebra with exchange matrix $B$. Its exchange graph is the graph whose vertices are seeds and whose edges join seeds related by mutation; it carries a canonical connection matching mutations in the same cluster direction across an edge. **Exchange-graph independence conjecture.** The exchange graph of $\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}, B)$, together with its canonical connection, depends only on $B$. This is a strengthening of the fact that the exchange graph depends only on the underlying $Y$-pattern. It is proved for cluster algebras of finite type, but the general statement remains open.
379564.source_name: Sergey Fomin and Andrei Zelevinsky, “Cluster algebras IV: Coefficients”, arXiv:math/0602259 (2006).
379564.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602259

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2006). “For cluster algebras of finite type, Conjecture was proved in .”

379601.title: Ghrist's conjecture on planar graph braid groups
379601.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a planar graph, and let $B_n\Gamma$ and $P B_n\Gamma$ denote its $n$-strand braid group and pure braid group, respectively. A group is **right-angled Artin** if it admits a presentation whose defining relators are commutators of pairs of generators. **Ghrist's conjecture.** The (pure) braid group of any planar graph is a right-angled Artin group. The conjecture is significant because it predicts a particularly tractable algebraic structure for braid groups arising from planar graphs. The paper gives counterexamples, so the conjecture is refuted.
379601.source_name: Daniel Farley and Lucas Sabalka, “On the cohomology rings of tree braid groups”, arXiv:math/0602444 (2007).
379601.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602444

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2006); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

379613.title: Nešetřil's Pentagon Conjecture for high-girth cubic graphs
379613.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph and let its girth be the length of its shortest cycle. A graph homomorphism $G\to C_5$ is a vertex map preserving adjacency.

**Nešetřil's Pentagon Conjecture.** If $G$ is a cubic graph of sufficiently high girth, then $G$ is homomorphic to $C_5$.

Equivalently, sufficiently high-girth cubic graphs should have circular chromatic number at most $5/2$. The statement is known with $C_3$ in place of $C_5$, while replacing $C_5$ by $C_7$ is false; the Pentagon Conjecture itself remains open.
379613.source_name: Matt DeVos and Robert Samal, “High-girth cubic graphs are homomorphic to the Clebsch graph”, arXiv:math/0602580 (2009).
379613.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602580

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2006). “This case was resolved in the affirmative by Naserasr who deduced it from a theorem of Guenin .”

379618.title: The symmetrization conjecture for Rayleigh partition functions
379618.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set of size $m$, let $\omega$ be a weight function, and let $Z(\omega;\mathbf y)$ be its partition function. Define the symmetrized weight and partition function by

$$
\widetilde Z(\omega;\mathbf y)=\frac1{m!}\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_m}Z(\omega;\mathbf y_\sigma).
$$

**Symmetrization conjecture.** If $Z(\omega;\mathbf y)$ is Rayleigh, then $\widetilde Z(\omega;\mathbf y)$ is Rayleigh. This is stated as an equivalent form of the Big Conjecture and remains open.
379618.source_name: David G. Wagner, “Negatively correlated random variables and Mason's conjecture”, arXiv:math/0602648 (2006).
379618.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602648

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2006). “A positive solution to the Big Conjecture would be a very good thing.”

379628.title: Squared-binomial triangle satisfies conditions (C1) and (C2)
379628.statement:
Consider the triangular array with entries $\binom{n}{k}^2$ for $0\leq k\leq n$. Conditions (C1) and (C2) are the two conditions imposed on a triangular array in the source's theorem on q-log-convexity. **Squared-binomial triangle conjecture.** The triangle

$$
\left\{\binom{n}{k}^2\right\}
$$

satisfies conditions (C1) and (C2) in that theorem. The claim is proposed in connection with the central binomial coefficients and central Delannoy numbers, but the supplied context does not state the conditions explicitly or report any verification.
379628.source_name: Li Liu and Yi Wang, “On the log-convexity of combinatorial sequences”, arXiv:math/0602672 (2006).
379628.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602672

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2006).

379662.title: The K-theoretic matroid invariant conjecture
379662.statement:
Let $M$, $M_1$, and $M_2$ be matroids, with $M^\perp$ denoting the dual matroid, $M_1\oplus M_2$ their direct sum, and $M_1+_2M_2$ their parallel connection. Let $g_M(t)\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be the matroid invariant defined in the paper.

**K-theoretic matroid invariant conjecture.** For any matroids $M$, $M_1$, and $M_2$,

$$
g_M=g_{M^\perp},\qquad g_{M_1\oplus M_2}=g_{M_1}g_{M_2},\qquad g_{M_1+_2M_2}=t g_{M_1}g_{M_2},
$$

and all coefficients of $g_M$ are nonnegative.

The conjecture is proposed to extend the results from realizable matroids to matroids realizable only in positive characteristic or not realizable at all. No resolution evidence is supplied, so it remains open.
379662.source_name: David E Speyer, “A matroid invariant via the K-theory of the Grassmannian”, arXiv:math/0603551 (2006).
379662.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0603551

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2006).

379692.title: Whitehead graph feature-region conjecture
379692.statement: Let $F$ be a free group, and associate to each element of $F$ the feature vector of weights of its Whitehead Graph in the corresponding feature space. A **region** is a bounded subset of that space whose boundary can be described by a hypersurface. **Whitehead graph feature-region conjecture.** These feature vectors are separated into bounded regions, each of which can be bounded by a hypersurface and corresponds to a particular Nielsen automorphism, in the sense that all elements in the corresponding class can be reduced by that automorphism. The conjecture is explicitly described as vague and is proposed as a model for the behavior of non-minimal elements; the source provides experimental motivation but no proof or resolution.
379692.source_name: R. M. Haralick, A. D. Miasnikov and A. G. Myasnikov, “Heuristics for The Whitehead Minimization Problem”, arXiv:math/0604204 (2006).
379692.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0604204

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2006).

379757.title: The tropical halfspace representation conjecture for pure tropical polytopes
379757.statement:
Let $P$ be a tropical polytope, let $\overline{P}$ be a lift of $P$, and call the lift **generic** when it satisfies the genericity condition used in the source. Call $P$ **pure** when all of its maximal cells have the same dimension, and call $P$ **generic** when it satisfies the source's genericity condition.

**Tropical halfspace representation conjecture.** If $P$ is pure, then the halfspaces from a generic lift $\overline{P}$ of $P$ map to tropical halfspaces whose intersection is $P$ itself. If, in addition, $P$ is generic, then any lift works.

The preceding proposition proves the assertion under the additional hypothesis that the relevant intersection of tropical halfspaces is pure; the conjecture asserts that this purity conclusion holds in general.
379757.source_name: Mike Develin and Josephine Yu, “Tropical polytopes and cellular resolutions”, arXiv:math/0605494 (2006).
379757.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605494

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2006).

379761.title: Green–Konyagin–Littlewood conjecture for the Fourier algebra norm
379761.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number and let $A\subset\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ have density bounded away from $0$ and $1$ by an absolute constant. **Green–Konyagin–Littlewood conjecture.** Then

$$
\|\chi_A\|_{A(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})}\gg\log p.
$$

This strengthens the lower bound proved by Green and Konyagin, replacing an order of $(\log p/\log\log p)^{1/3}$ with the conjectured logarithmic growth. The source presents the claim as a conjecture and gives no resolution.
379761.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605522

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2006).

379764.title: De Simone–Körner conjecture on hereditary normality of graphs
379764.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A graph is **hereditarily normal** if every induced subgraph of $G$ is normal, where a graph is normal when it has coverings by cliques and stable sets such that every clique in one covering intersects every stable set in the other. An induced subgraph is a **5-cycle** or **7-cycle** when it is isomorphic to the corresponding cycle graph.

**De Simone–Körner conjecture.** A graph $G$ is hereditarily normal if and only if neither $G$ nor its complement contains a 5-cycle or a 7-cycle as an induced subgraph.

The conjecture aims to characterize hereditary normality by the two known minimal obstructions, the 5-cycle, the 7-cycle, and the complement of the 7-cycle. The source gives no resolution status.
379764.source_name: Zsolt Patakfalvi, “Line-graphs of cubic graphs are normal”, arXiv:math/0605568 (2006).
379764.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0605568

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2006).

379801.title: The intrinsic virtual knotting conjecture for intrinsically knotted graphs
379801.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Call $G$ **intrinsically knotted** if every classical spatial embedding of $G$ contains a non-trivial knot, and call it **intrinsically virtually knotted of degree 1** if every virtual diagram of $G$ with at most one virtual crossing contains a virtually knotted cycle. **Intrinsic virtual knotting conjecture.** If $G$ is intrinsically knotted, then $G$ is intrinsically virtually knotted of degree $1$.

The conjecture is motivated by the claim that the Jones polynomial distinguishes the unknot. The stated theorem proves the conclusion under the additional hypothesis that every diagram of $G$ contains a knot with non-trivial Jones polynomial; the unrestricted assertion remains open in the supplied text.
379801.source_name: Thomas Fleming and Blake Mellor, “Intrinsic Linking and Knotting in Virtual Spatial Graphs”, arXiv:math/0606231 (2006).
379801.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0606231

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2006). “A counterexample to this conjecture would also be an example of a non-trivial knot with trivial Jones polynomial.”

379878.title: Width conjecture for triangle-polygon graphs
379878.statement:
Let $P_{t,k}=P_3|P_k$ be the graph with $k+1$ vertices obtained by gluing a triangle and a $k$-gon along an edge. Let $w^1_{{\mathcal A}_3}(G)$ be the width of the torsion in $H^{1,*}_{{\mathcal A}_3}(G)$, namely the maximal torsion grading minus the minimal torsion grading, with value $-1$ when all cohomology is free. **Width conjecture for $P_{t,k}$.** For these graphs,

$$
w^1_{{\mathcal A}_3}(P_{t,k})=k-3.
$$

The formula is based on the displayed computations for this family; the source does not state a resolution.
379878.source_name: Milena D. Pabiniak, Jozef H. Przytycki and Radmila Sazdanovic, “On the first group of the chromatic cohomology of graphs”, arXiv:math/0607326 (2006).
379878.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607326

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2006). “This is still an open problem, and motivated by this we thought that for $\A_3$ graph homology torsion will be rather limited.”

379928.title: The local square-energy conjecture in logarithmic intervals
379928.statement:
For a finite set $E$ of squares in the short interval

$$
E\subset\{k^2:N\le k\le N+N/(\log N)^\delta\},
$$

let $r_{E+E}(m)$ count representations of $m$ as a sum of two elements of $E$. **The local energy conjecture.** There exists $\delta>0$ such that

$$
\sum_m r_{E+E}^2(m)\ll |E|^2.
$$

The source introduces this as the special square-polynomial case of the short interval conjectures and states that it remains open.
379928.source_name: Javier Cilleruelo and Andrew Granville, “Lattice points on circles, squares in arithmetic progressions and sumsets of squares”, arXiv:math/0608109 (2006).
379928.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608109

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).

379961.title: The seed-by-cluster conjecture for cluster algebras
379961.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}=\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S})$ be a normalized skew-symmetrizable cluster algebra, where $\mathcal{S}$ is a mutation equivalence class of seeds, and let a **cluster** mean the set of cluster variables in a seed. Two seeds belong to the same mutation equivalence class as prescribed by $\mathcal{S}$. **Seed-by-cluster conjecture.** Each seed in a cluster algebra is uniquely determined by its cluster. Two such seeds are related by a mutation if and only if the corresponding clusters share all elements but one. This conjecture would allow the exchange graph to be identified with the dual graph of the cluster complex, with adjacency determined by clusters whose intersection has cardinality $n-1$.
379961.source_name: Sergey Fomin, Michael Shapiro and Dylan Thurston, “Cluster algebras and triangulated surfaces. Part I: Cluster complexes”, arXiv:math/0608367 (2007).
379961.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608367

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).

379962.title: The flag-complex conjecture for cluster complexes
379962.statement: Let $\mathcal{A}=\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S})$ be a cluster algebra, let $\mathcal{X}$ be its set of cluster variables, and let the **cluster complex** be the simplicial complex on $\mathcal{X}$ whose maximal simplices are the clusters. Two cluster variables are **compatible** if they appear together in some cluster. **Flag-complex conjecture.** The cluster complex is always a flag complex: it is the clique complex for the compatibility relation on the set of all cluster variables. The assertion says that every pairwise compatible collection of cluster variables belongs to a common cluster, so the complex is determined by its one-skeleton.
379962.source_name: Sergey Fomin, Michael Shapiro and Dylan Thurston, “Cluster algebras and triangulated surfaces. Part I: Cluster complexes”, arXiv:math/0608367 (2007).
379962.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608367

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).

380468.title: Shibuya's boundary-link conjecture for self Delta-equivalence
380468.statement: Let an oriented link be a **boundary link** if its components bound pairwise disjoint Seifert surfaces in $S^3$. Let the **trivial link** be the link whose components are disjoint unknotted circles bounding disjoint disks. Two links are self $\Delta$-equivalent when they are transformed into each other by self delta moves and ambient isotopies, with all three strings in each move belonging to the same component. **Shibuya's conjecture.** Any boundary link is self $\Delta$-equivalent to the trivial link. This conjecture predicts that self Delta-equivalence detects no further obstruction for boundary links beyond their boundary-link structure; the supplied text gives no resolution.
380468.source_name: Ryo Nikkuni, “Delta edge-homotopy invariants of spatial graphs via disk-summing the constituent knots”, arXiv:math/0703319 (2007).
380468.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0703319

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2007).
